messages:
sam: Heads-up — getting a customer escalation: APAC region p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~120ms to 780ms starting ~02:10 UTC. Multiple customers reporting timeouts and slow TLS handshakes. Can someone pick this up?

opsbot: alert: service.generate.p99.apac >= 700ms at 2026-03-17T02:12:05Z. Affected POPs: apac1, apac2. See /dash/alerts/9182

mira: On it. I see a concurrent spike in egress RTT from apac1 to our us-east egress (we fall back during capacity bursts). Traceroutes from apac1 show an extra cross-az hop.

jules: Do we have recent routing changes? I didn't see infra deploy but cloud provider had a route redistribution at 02:05 UTC in apac region. Could be GSLB decision moving traffic to a different backbone.

sam: Customer says TLS handshake latency specifically — looks like SYN->ACK fine but TLS handshake RTT is the extra 600ms. Could be MTU/path or middlebox rehandshake.

mira: Ran a quick curl from apac1 edge to model host via the path with tcpdump. Here's the timing sketch:
```
TCP connect: 40ms
TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello: 620ms
Application data start: 630ms
```
Not seeing retransmits but server's ServerHello delayed. Maybe the request hit a warm standby that was scaling up?

carter: I pulled edge logs for the timeframe. apac1 shows a small surge in connections hitting a fallback pool (fallback_pool_b) configured for burst overflow. That pool is hosted in a different AZ and has higher cold-starts on TLS handshakes (we've seen ~500-700ms for fresh connections before).

jules: That matches. Why was traffic routed to fallback_pool_b? Autoscaler should have handled scaling in primary pool. Any recent change to autoscaler thresholds?

mira: No config changes in autoscaler. I suspect the cloud NLB had transient capacity pressure and our smart-routing policy opted to spill to fallback. Need to confirm with provider support. Opening ticket now.

opsbot: ticket created: CSP-5543 "APAC egress route spill -> fallback_pool_b causing TLS p99 regressions" assigned to cloud-support.

sam: Short term mitigation: can we force routing to prefer primary pool (even temporarily) to avoid cold TLS stalls? Or enable short-lived TLS session caching on fallback nodes?

carter: Quick mitigation options I can do: 1) raise prefer_primary weight to 90% for apac1 (instant but will reduce burst capacity), 2) pre-warm TLS endpoints in fallback_pool_b (kick connections via probe) — takes ~30s to warm. Which do we prefer?

jules: Let's do both: raise prefer_primary now, and kick TLS pre-warm probes to fallback nodes. If provider fix arrives we can revert weight.

mira: I'll coordinate the provider ticket and keep monitoring. Adding synthetic p99 probe at 10s cadence to apac1->model-host to watch TLS handshake time.

sam: Sounds good. Notify support and affected customers with ETA ~15-30m. Post follow-up when p99 drops. :thumbsup:

carter: Done: prefer_primary weight bumped to 90% for apac1 at 02:18 UTC. Pre-warm probes started (7/7 nodes warmed). Observability shows p99 dropping to ~140ms after ~45s.

mira: Provider replied: transient routing churn due to upstream spine maintenance; they confirmed some flows were diverted through a different backbone resulting in cross-AZ hop. They will backfill capacity; monitoring for further regressions.

sam: Great—closing loop with customers. Action items: (1) add fallback pool TLS warmup during autoscaler spill events, (2) add automated rollback to traffic weights if p99 rises, (3) update runbook with these steps. I'll file follow-ups.

opsbot: incident-note: mitigated 2026-03-17T02:19:30Z, monitoring for 30m. CSP-5543 -> status: monitoring.
